title: I built a game with AI, then used AI to overhaul its visuals.
author: Dependent-Video7534
selftext:
Hi everyone! Back in April, I used Claude to help develop a zombie tower defense game and released it on Steam.

I was using Opus 4.7 at the time. Many of the visual effects were fairly basic, and the character animations had very few frames, so the overall presentation looked a bit rough.

Recently, I revisited the game with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 to improve its visuals. I’ve been pleasantly surprised by how much AI-assisted development has progressed. With their help, I’ve been able to improve the character animations, pixel-style effects, and UI design.

There’s still room for improvement, but I’m much happier with how the game looks now compared to the original version.

  
Old  version：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ADej31QogVU  


If you’re curious, there’s a free demo on Steam. I’d love to hear what you think of the updated visuals.

STEAM PAGE：https://store.steampowered.com/app/4609110/BULLET\_GIRLZOMBIE\_DEFENSE/?beta=0

comments.author: simon_is_high
comments.body: Darf ich fragen wie dein Workflow war um so konsistente Animationen zu bekommen?

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body: I use GPT and Gemini’s image generation tools to create the characters and some action poses, then use Ludo to turn them into animations.

replies.author: simon_is_high
replies.body: Oooh thank you so much! Never heard of Ludo but thats exactly what Im looking for

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body: This could actually work if you had more stages and a story line.

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body: Thanks for the valuable feedback! I’m planning to add more stages and new game modes featuring elite enemies, but everything is still in the planning phase.

replies.author: Jolly-Rip5973
replies.body:
Not sure if you have ever played Nikke: Goddess of Victory. 

But making each of your units actually have a bit of back story, maybe simple cut scenes between stages of the girls interacting, stages progressing in a story line and some world building would make the game far more interesting. 

Something like stage 2 involves level at strip club or poker casino and this unlocks the bunnygirl with the axe.   
Stage 3 could involve a mansion and this is where you unlock the maid character.   
Stage 4 involves a hospital and this is where you unlock the nurse character. 

Just ignore the fact that you making multiple copies of each character during the game play, but give each character a name, backstory, a bit of personality and make them likable. 

at least in the theory each character should be a waifu. You can even look up waifu personality types and use an AI to develop the cut scene dialog and personality types of each girl.  

You could simply have an option to the skip the cut scenes so they aren't annoying in a second play through. 

Then add a procedural rogue like stages on the end of the game for some end game content. Have a ladder system in the end game content so you can try to break a record for surviving the most stages in the end game.   
  
You would only procedural content in the end game though since some end game stages you might be bad rolls and they could simply be overwhelming.   
  
You want tight level design on the story stages for tweaked difficulty to finish the story stages.

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body: Thank you so much! I do know Nikke, and this is a really great suggestion. I think it could apply to pretty much any game like this. I'll think seriously about how to approach it next. Thanks again!

replies.author: Jolly-Rip5973
replies.body:
cool. would love to see what you do with it.   
I would make the girls a little more fan service like too. You don't have to over do it though.
